page: Microsoft Azure D64als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dalv6 server family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The configuration includes 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. Cache resources consist of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a low-memory profile of 2.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench multi-core performance and image processing. It demonstrates strong performance across stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, Passmark CPU metrics, and cryptographic operations, aided by hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient for small cached blocks, though uncached large-block reads fall into the average tier. Multi-threaded decompression and Redis SET operations also register in the top 25% of tested systems, alongside strong throughput for static web serving and small-to-medium LLM inference tasks.

The primary tradeoff of the D64als_v6 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and the complete absence of local storage. This makes it highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive in-memory datasets or local scratch disks. It is well-suited for parallel processing tasks, software compilation, image processing, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression workloads.

It is powered by a dedicated 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 64 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Benchmarks place this server in the top 10% for Geekbench multi-core and image processing, with strong top-25% performance in multi-core stress tests, cryptography, and static web serving. The lack of local storage and lower memory density represent key design tradeoffs, making this server highly cost-efficient for compute-dense, non-memory-intensive workloads such as software compilation, parallel processing, and web serving.
